pubcol-w-4ffba260e3975da2.definition_en: to gain an advantage over someone
collocations: get the start of a rival
get the start of the competition
get the start of an opponent
pubcol-w-4ffba260e3975da2.example_simple: She got the start of the other runners and never lost her lead.
pubcol-w-4ffba260e3975da2.example_complex: By filing their patent months earlier, the firm got the start of every competitor in the emerging market.
pubcol-w-4ffba260e3975da2.vi_meaning_correction: chiếm được lợi thế hơn ai

pubcol-w-e1b1da6f6888f24a.definition_en: to start or continue communicating with someone regularly
collocations: keep in touch with old friends
get in touch with a colleague
pubcol-w-e1b1da6f6888f24a.example_simple: We promised to keep in touch with each other after graduation.
pubcol-w-e1b1da6f6888f24a.example_complex: Despite living on different continents, they managed to keep in touch with one another through weekly video calls.

pubcol-w-466f80a7d98af94e.definition_en: to complete a course of study and be awarded a qualification
pubcol-w-466f80a7d98af94e.example_simple: She worked hard to get a degree in engineering.
pubcol-w-466f80a7d98af94e.example_complex: After years of evening classes, he finally got a diploma in accounting that opened new career doors.

pubcol-w-f8a580fa38b93a72.definition_en: to be moved to a more senior job or position
pubcol-w-f8a580fa38b93a72.example_simple: He hopes to get a promotion by the end of the year.
pubcol-w-f8a580fa38b93a72.example_complex: After leading the project to success, she got a promotion to head of the department.

pubcol-w-f154dffd740820cc.definition_en: to be given an increase in pay
pubcol-w-f154dffd740820cc.example_simple: She was happy to get a raise after her review.
pubcol-w-f154dffd740820cc.example_complex: Employees who consistently exceed their targets are far more likely to get a raise than those who merely meet them.

pubcol-w-7b0eaa676aa77fe2.definition_en: to obtain an outcome or effect produced by something
collocations: get a result from an experiment
get a result from hard work
get a result from the treatment
pubcol-w-7b0eaa676aa77fe2.example_simple: You won't get a result from the test until tomorrow.
pubcol-w-7b0eaa676aa77fe2.example_complex: Researchers were surprised to get such a clear result from a study that used only a small sample.

pubcol-w-e7e0a90bb3cfb1a4.definition_en: to regain energy and enthusiasm after feeling tired
synonyms: get a fresh burst of energy
collocations: get a second wind at night
get a second wind halfway through
pubcol-w-e7e0a90bb3cfb1a4.example_simple: I was exhausted, but I got a second wind after a short break.
pubcol-w-e7e0a90bb3cfb1a4.example_complex: Just when the marathon runners seemed spent, many got a second wind in the final stretch and surged toward the finish.
pubcol-w-e7e0a90bb3cfb1a4.vi_meaning_correction: lấy lại được sức lực để tiếp tục làm

pubcol-w-cde58f8b8b3273be.definition_en: to hear a piece of information, especially a secret or rumour
pubcol-w-cde58f8b8b3273be.example_simple: The press got wind of the deal before it was announced.
pubcol-w-cde58f8b8b3273be.example_complex: As soon as competitors got wind of the merger talks, the company's share price began to fluctuate wildly.
pubcol-w-cde58f8b8b3273be.vi_meaning_correction: nghe phong thanh, nghe lỏm được

pubcol-w-5232d5f548e39b41.definition_en: to perform music for an audience at an organised event
collocations: give a concert in the park
pubcol-w-5232d5f548e39b41.example_simple: The orchestra will give a concert next Saturday.
pubcol-w-5232d5f548e39b41.example_complex: To raise money for the flood victims, several famous bands agreed to give a concert in the city stadium.

pubcol-w-3d42a9e009ff8adc.definition_en: to help someone do a task
collocations: give a hand with the dishes
pubcol-w-3d42a9e009ff8adc.example_simple: Could you give me a hand with these boxes?
pubcol-w-3d42a9e009ff8adc.example_complex: Whenever the neighbours were struggling, he was always the first to give a hand with whatever needed doing.

pubcol-w-757ea1ae20391e8b.definition_en: to spend time thinking or considering something
collocations: give a thought to the future
give some thought to the idea
pubcol-w-757ea1ae20391e8b.example_simple: Have you given any thought to where you want to study?
pubcol-w-757ea1ae20391e8b.example_complex: Before accepting the offer, she gave careful thought to how the move would affect her family.

pubcol-w-47bbbccbb846b731.definition_en: a willingness of each side to make concessions in a relationship or negotiation
collocations: a spirit of give and take
pubcol-w-47bbbccbb846b731.example_simple: Every good marriage needs some give and take.
pubcol-w-47bbbccbb846b731.example_complex: Successful negotiations depend on a degree of give and take, with neither party expecting to win every point.

pubcol-w-99e7335368f1abe2.definition_en: to produce a baby; also to cause something to begin
pubcol-w-99e7335368f1abe2.example_simple: She gave birth to a healthy baby girl.
pubcol-w-99e7335368f1abe2.example_complex: The Industrial Revolution gave birth to social changes whose effects are still felt today.

pubcol-w-db1766d73a3d93b0.definition_en: to yield or retreat under pressure; to make concessions
pubcol-w-db1766d73a3d93b0.example_simple: Neither side would give ground during the argument.
pubcol-w-db1766d73a3d93b0.example_complex: The government refused to give ground on immigration policy despite mounting pressure from the opposition.

pubcol-w-eee2d5bc82e04b7d.definition_en: to allow someone to do something
pubcol-w-eee2d5bc82e04b7d.example_simple: My parents gave me permission to go to the party.
pubcol-w-eee2d5bc82e04b7d.example_complex: The council eventually gave permission for the new development after months of public consultation.

pubcol-w-fbd937873e2a7b5f.definition_en: to yield a profit; also, to give someone a gift
pubcol-w-fbd937873e2a7b5f.example_simple: We gave her a present for her birthday.
pubcol-w-fbd937873e2a7b5f.example_complex: The investment gave a steady profit, and to celebrate they gave every employee a present at the end of the year.
pubcol-w-fbd937873e2a7b5f.vi_meaning_correction: sinh lãi; tặng quà cho ai

pubcol-w-bd90ae39435d7301.definition_en: to take someone somewhere in your vehicle
collocations: give sb a lift to work
give sb a ride to the station
pubcol-w-bd90ae39435d7301.example_simple: Can you give me a lift to the airport tomorrow?
pubcol-w-bd90ae39435d7301.example_complex: Since it was pouring with rain, a kind stranger offered to give the stranded tourists a lift into town.

pubcol-w-3b66946c641766c6.definition_en: to take someone somewhere in your vehicle
collocations: give sb a lift to work
give sb a ride to the station
pubcol-w-3b66946c641766c6.example_simple: She kindly gave me a lift to the bus station.
pubcol-w-3b66946c641766c6.example_complex: He often gives his elderly neighbour a lift to the clinic when her son is away.

pubcol-w-b111b3008721738e.definition_en: to promise someone firmly that something is true or will happen
pubcol-w-b111b3008721738e.example_simple: He gave me his assurance that the work would be finished on time.
pubcol-w-b111b3008721738e.example_complex: The minister gave the public his assurance that the new safety measures would be fully funded.

pubcol-w-5ae72a7324045caa.ipa: /ɡɪv ˈsʌmθɪŋ ə njuː liːs əv laɪf/
pubcol-w-5ae72a7324045caa.definition_en: to renew or restore something so that it lasts longer or works better
collocations: give the building a new lease of life
give a new lease of life to the town
give the engine a new lease of life
pubcol-w-5ae72a7324045caa.example_simple: A fresh coat of paint gave the old house a new lease of life.
pubcol-w-5ae72a7324045caa.example_complex: The regeneration project gave the run-down harbour a new lease of life, drawing tourists and businesses back to the area.
